evidence.paraphrase: The narrator recalls being horrified by witnessing Grimlan's violent seizure.
evidence.quote: I had been appalled at the writhings, howlings and yammerings of the wretch, who had groveled on the earth like a wounded snake, gibbering terrible curses and black blasphemies until his voice broke in a wordless screaming which spattered his lips with foam.

evidence.paraphrase: Conrad offers a medical, hereditary-disease explanation for Grimlan's condition.
evidence.quote: Old John doubtless fell heir to some ingrown weakness brought on by some loathsome disease, which was his heritage from perhaps a remote ancestor--such things occasionally happen.

evidence.paraphrase: Conrad proposes that Grimlan caught an unclassified tropical disease during his travels.
evidence.quote: It is quite possible that he was infected with some obscure malady in his wanderings. There are still many unclassified diseases in Africa and the Orient.

evidence.paraphrase: Conrad describes systematically investigating Grimlan's history by questioning villagers.
evidence.quote: I have been at pains to inquire about him discreetly," said Conrad. "He has lived here--with the exception of mysterious absences often for months at a time--for twenty years.

evidence.paraphrase: Grimlan is reported to have not aged over twenty years, appearing about fifty throughout.
evidence.quote: they all say that in the intervening years he seems not to have aged perceptibly. When he came here he looked just as he does now--or did, up to the moment of his death--of the appearance of a man about fifty.

evidence.paraphrase: An elderly professor recalls Grimlan looking fifty fifty years earlier, implying he has not aged.
evidence.quote: he knew Grimlan when a very young man studying in Berlin, fifty years ago, and he expressed astonishment that the old man was still living; for he said at that time Grimlan seemed to be about fifty years of age.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator rationalizes the aging anomaly while physically recoiling in dread.
evidence.quote: Professor Von Boehnk is past eighty himself, and liable to the errors of extreme age. He confused this man with another." Yet as I spoke, my flesh crawled unpleasantly and the hairs on my neck prickled.

evidence.paraphrase: A genealogy record dates Grimlan's birth to 1630 and his death to 1930, spanning three centuries.
evidence.quote: John Grymlann, borne, March 10, 1630." And then we both cried out. Under this entry was freshly written, in a strange scrawling hand, "Died, March 10, 1930.

evidence.paraphrase: Grimlan's own written incantation states he was fifty years old in 1680.
evidence.quote: beinge of rite mynd & fiftie years of age this yeare of 1680, A.D.

evidence.paraphrase: The incantation describes a bargain granting an unnaturally extended lifespan of 250 years.
evidence.quote: for a price maye he gain hys heartes desire, ryches & knowledge beyond countinge & lyffe beyond mortal span even two hundred & fiftie yeares.

evidence.paraphrase: When the final candle goes out, an inhuman cry and chaos erupt in the dark room.
evidence.quote: The last candle went out suddenly and a ghastly unhuman cry that came not from my lips or from Conrad's burst unbearably forth.

evidence.paraphrase: The corpse and the oriental visitor vanish from a still-locked room.
evidence.quote: showed us the black ebony table--empty! The doors and windows were locked as they had been, but the oriental was gone--and so was the corpse of John Grimlan.

evidence.paraphrase: The house is rapidly consumed by fire into a blazing inferno.
evidence.quote: Flames had enveloped the whole house with appalling swiftness, and now the great mass was etched against the shadowed sky, a crimson inferno.

evidence.paraphrase: Conrad cries out interpreting the events as the collection of a 250-year-old demonic bargain.
evidence.quote: Soul and body he sold to Malik Tous, who is Satan, two hundred and fifty years ago! This was the night of payment--and my God--look!

evidence.paraphrase: A huge bat-like shadow carries off a man-shaped body above the burning house.
evidence.quote: above the holocaust hovered a gigantic black shadow like a monstrous bat, and from its dark clutch dangled a small white thing, like the body of a man, dangling limply.
